Provide
pro-VYDE
v.
From Latin providere, to see beforehand, to foresee — the same root as providence. Webster 1828: to procure beforehand; to get, collect or make ready for future use. The etymology is the doctrine: God provides because God foresees, and Abraham named a mountain after it.

Biblical Definition

Provide and providence are the same word, and Genesis 22 is where Scripture makes the connexion unforgettable. Climbing Moriah with the wood on his son’s back, Isaac asks where the lamb is, and Abraham answers, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together (Genesis 22:8). A ram is caught in a thicket, and the father names the place: Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen (Genesis 22:14). The margin gives the sense — the LORD will see, or provide — and centuries later, on that same range of hills, God did provide Himself a Lamb, His own Son. The word also carries a hard human duty. Paul writes: if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel (1 Timothy 5:8). And it governs public integrity: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men (Romans 12:17) — a Christian is to take thought beforehand for how his conduct will look, not to court approval but because the gospel’s reputation is bound to his.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines PROVIDE as to procure beforehand; to get, collect or make ready for future use; to prepare; to furnish; to supply; and notes the Latin origin in providere, to foresee. The forethought is in the word itself.

expand to see more

PROVIDE, v.t. — To procure beforehand; to get, collect or make ready for future use; to prepare.

To furnish; to supply; followed by with before the thing supplied.

To stipulate previously; as, the law provides for this case.

PROVIDE, v.i. — To take measures beforehand; as, to provide against the evils of a siege.

From Latin pro, before, and videre, to see — the same compound that gives providence and prudence.

Key Scripture

Genesis 22:8 — "And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together."

Genesis 22:14 — "And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen."

1 Timothy 5:8 — "But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel."

Romans 12:17 — "Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men."

Matthew 6:33 — "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."

Modern Corruption

Providence has been reduced in popular usage to a vague benevolence and in practice to good luck; Scripture’s word means God seeing beforehand and acting accordingly, and Genesis 22 shows it costing Him His own Son.

expand to see more

God will provide himself a lamb is one of the great sentences of the Old Testament, and it is spoken by a father walking uphill with a knife and a son who has just asked the unanswerable question. Abraham does not know how; Hebrews says he accounted that God was able to raise him up even from the dead. What arrives is a ram caught by its horns — a substitute, not a rescue — and the name given the place points forward rather than back: in the mount of the LORD it shall be seen. The Reformed doctrine of providence is not the belief that things generally work out. It is the belief that God governs all His creatures and all their actions to His own ends, and Moriah is the place where that doctrine and the doctrine of substitutionary atonement are shown to be the same thing.

1 Timothy 5:8 will not let the doctrine float free of the household budget. A man who does not provide for his own has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel — language Paul uses nowhere else about a failure of ordinary duty, and he uses it because the unbeliever manages this much by natural affection. Trust in providence is never a substitute for provision; the same God who feeds the ravens gave Joseph seven years to fill the storehouses. And Romans 12:17 extends the forethought outward: a Christian is to arrange his affairs so that they will bear inspection, because things honest in the sight of all men is part of not giving occasion to the adversary.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ra’ah (H7200), to see, and so to provide — the verb behind Jehovahjireh; Greek pronoeo (G4306), to think of beforehand, in 1 Timothy 5:8 and Romans 12:17.

expand to see more

Hebrew ra’ah (H7200) — to see, to look upon, and by extension to provide; Genesis 22:8, 14.

Hebrew YHWH yireh — Jehovahjireh, the LORD will see or provide; the name Abraham gave the mount.

Greek pronoeo (G4306) — to perceive before, to provide for; 1 Timothy 5:8, Romans 12:17, 2 Corinthians 8:21.

Greek pronoia (G4307) — forethought, provision; the Greek noun standing behind the theological term providence.

Latin providere — to see beforehand; the source of both provide and providence in English.

Usage

"God will provide himself a lamb (Genesis 22:8) — spoken on the way up Moriah, and fulfilled on it."

"If any provide not for his own… he hath denied the faith (1 Timothy 5:8) — the household duty stated at full strength."

"Provide things honest in the sight of all men (Romans 12:17) — forethought about a Christian’s public integrity."
